title: Ensure 'Configure the 'Block at First Sight' feature' is set to 'Enabled'
description: This policy setting configures whether the device checks (in real time) with the Microsoft Active Protection Service (MAPS) before allowing certain content to be run or accessed. Rationale: Enabling the Block at First Sight feature enhances threat protection by using next-generation protection to detect new malware and block it within seconds. title: Ensure 'Trigger a quick scan after X days without any scans' is set to 'Enabled: 7'
description: This policy setting configures the number of days after the last scan (of any type) before an aggressive Quick Scan is automatically triggered. The recommended state for this setting is: Enabled: 7 days. Audit reads the Group Policy registry value and prints 'compliant', 'unset' (policy not configured, reported as FAIL) or the non-compliant value. title: Ensure 'Turn on e-mail scanning' is set to 'Enabled'
description: This policy setting configures e-mail scanning. When e-mail scanning is enabled, the engine will parse the mailbox and mail files, according to their specific format, to analyze the mail bodies and attachments. Several e-mail formats are currently supported, for example: pst (Outlook), dbx, mbx, mime (Outlook Express), binhex (Mac). The recommended state for this setting is: Enabled. Rationale: All emails should be scanned by an antivirus solution such as Microsoft Defender Antivirus, as email attachments are a commonly used attack vector to infiltrate computers with malicious software. title: Ensure 'Specify the interval to check for security intelligence updates' is set to 'Enabled: 4' or fewer, but not '0'
description: This policy setting configures an interval at which to check for security intelligence updates. Security intelligence updates are the continuously updated packages that Microsoft Defender Antivirus uses to recognize, classify, and block the latest malware, spyware, unwanted software, and potentially harmful behaviors. The recommended state for this setting is: Enabled: 4 or fewer, but not 0. Rationale: A malware scan is only as effective as the threat definitions it uses. Running a scan with outdated intelligence significantly reduces detection accuracy and can create a false sense of security. Audit reads the Group Policy registry value and prints 'compliant', 'unset' (policy not configured, reported as FAIL) or the non-compliant value. The recommended state for this setting is: Enabled: Block. title: Ensure 'Turn off routine remediation' is set to 'Disabled'
description: This policy setting configures whether Microsoft Defender Antivirus automatically takes action on all detected threats. The action to be taken on a particular threat is determined by the combination of the policy-defined action, user-defined action, and the signature- defined action. The recommended state for this setting is: Disabled. Rationale: If this setting is enabled, Microsoft Defender prompts the user to take action on detected threats. Allowing users to choose threat remediation actions is not considered a best practice, as it can lead to inconsistent or unsafe responses. Audit reads the Group Policy registry value and prints 'compliant', 'unset' (policy not configured, reported as FAIL) or the non-compliant value. Remediation writes 0 locally; in a domain set it through the ADMX so Group Policy does not revert it.
